about.title: Kingsburg Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Kingsburg is a small city, but its main corridors carry a lot of local traffic — Mountain View Avenue, Sierra Street, Simpson Street, and Draper Street see regular travel from residents heading to school, work, or downtown. Fresno County recorded 20 injury collisions here in the most recent final year, hurting 30 people and taking 2 lives. Crashes here tend to cluster on Friday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m., a pattern that lines up with end-of-week commutes and weekend errands. If you were injured in one of these collisions, the days right after matter. Insurance adjusters move fast, and evidence like skid marks, damaged vehicles, and witness memory fades quickly. Our team can evaluate the crash, protect your rights, and handle the insurance company on your behalf while you focus on healing.

whyChoose.title: Why Act Quickly After a Kingsburg Crash

items.title: California's Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a personal injury lawsuit in California, but that window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity — like a city road crew or public bus — was involved. Waiting too long can cost you the ability to recover anything at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you were partly responsible for the collision, you can still pursue compensation reduced by your share of fault. We can help make sure the insurer doesn't inflate your percentage of blame to lower your payout.

items.title: Don't Give the Other Insurer a Recorded Statement
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement shortly after a crash, hoping to use your words against you later. You're not required to provide one, and speaking with us first can help protect your claim before you say anything that could be twisted.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Kingsburg?
items.answer: California generally allows two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government vehicle or a road defect maintained by a public entity was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth having us review your situation early.

items.question: What if the accident happened at a busy time, like a Friday afternoon on Simpson Street?
items.answer: Crash timing itself doesn't determine fault, but it can affect what evidence is available — traffic camera footage, witness availability, and even lighting conditions. We can help gather and preserve that evidence before it disappears, regardless of when or where in Kingsburg the crash occurred.

items.question: Will I owe anything upfront to talk to an attorney?
items.answer: No. We offer a free consultation, and we work on contingency, meaning we only get paid if your case results in a recovery. There's no upfront cost or obligation to contact us and ask questions.
